title: Russian rouble slips vs dollar,cbank reserves fall.
text:
MOSCOW, March 4 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble fell marginally against the dollar on Thursday as the central bank lowered its support floor for the national currency after selling over $1 billion from its reserves the previous session.  

The Russian currency for today settlement eased to 28.6653 per dollar from a weighted average of 28.5888 per dollar the previous session, when it shed about 10 kopecks in response to sharp gains by the greenback on global markets.  

Roubles for delivery on Friday fell to 28.72 per dollar in early hours of trade but rebounded to 28.6250 by 1050 GMT after the central bank sold $80-100 million to offset downward pressure on the local currency, dealers said.  

"The central bank's offer served as a signal it would not tolerate excessive volatility in the market. (The move) worked, and the rouble rebounded as banks apparently opted to re-open short positions," Sergei Romanchuk at Metallinvestbank said.  

Dealers said the central bank, which looked unwilling to run down its reserves ahead of $2.5 billion in foreign debt payments due in March, moved its offer to sell dollars to 28.6950 from 28.6350 on Wednesday, when it sold more than $1 billion.  

UFG investment house said the central bank's dollar selling interventions were nothing to worry about as Russia's solid balance of payments remained intact and no signs of major capital outflows were seen.  

The investment house suggested the rouble was likely to resume its upwards path after March 14 presidential elections thanks to high global crude prices and traditionally higher capital inflows in the second quarter of the year.  

"Market liquidity should hence remain strong until at least July, when seasonal worsening of the balance of payments usually kicks in," UFG said in its market comment.  

Also on Thursday, the central bank, which has been buying dollars from the market for most of last month to contain the rise of the rouble, reported its gold and foreign currency reserves shrank by $300 million to $86.4 billion on February 27.  

"It confirms market talk last week that the central bank was able to keep its interventions to a minimum, as market participants have begun to cover dollar shorts given month-long central bank support and euro/dollar weakness," Stanislav Gelfer, an analyst at 4Cast said.

title: Russia  c.bank  intervenes  as rouble marches upwards.
text:
MOSCOW, Oct 21 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble continued its upward stride on Tuesday on the back of forthcoming tax payments by companies, forcing the central bank to intervene to slow the rise, dealers said.   

The rouble firmed against the dollar in early official trade to a weighted average for tomorrow settlement of 29.9319 per dollar from 30.0179 in the previous session. By 1145 GMT roubles for settlement on Wednesday were traded at 29.9280.   

Dealers said the central bank had started intervening when the rouble for tomorrow delivery strengthened to 29.9150 and had so far sold about $60 million.   

"As expected, the dollar's fall continued but the central bank managed to curb it. Tax payments still affect the market," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexei Bukleyev.   

On Monday, the rouble broke through the psychologically important level of 30 but the central bank, which had intervened heavily to support the U.S. currency in previous weeks, abstained from the market then.   

"The dollar weakening against the rouble is justified and we can hardly expect the central bank to stop it," bank Trust said in a research note. "The central bank can only change the tempo but its instruments are limited because of inflationary consequences of its interventions."   

Moody's Investor Service awarded Russia an investment grade in early October, which opened doors to more foreign investment into the country. Strong prices for Russia's main exports, oil and gas, also increase the inflow of hard currency.

title: UPDATE 2-Russia cbank cuts refinancing rate by 300 bps.
text:
MOSCOW, Feb 14 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank on Friday announced a three percentage point cut in its refinancing rate in a move seen by analysts as guiding the market towards rouble rates more in line with those on hard currency instruments. 

 The bank said the rate would fall to 18 percent from 21 percent from February 17. 

 It made no comment on the move, which is in line with its strategy of regulating money supply through rates rather than intervention. 

 Commercial banks do not usually borrow from the central bank using the refinancing rate, but it is frequently used as a reference rate for overdue payments by banks and companies. 

 The central bank's foreign currency swaps, a popular instrument among banks to manage their rouble liquidity, are linked to an 18 percent overnight credit rate, which usually moves in line with the refinancing rate. 

 "The cut in the rate which currently plays a decorative role is of a psychological importance which is to guide the market towards lower rouble rates and bring them more in line with hard currency rates," Denis Rodionov, a director at Brunswick UBS Warburg. 

 Last week a senior central banker told Reuters he saw room for lowering the refinancing rate because of falling yields on the local debt market and said the central bank wanted to make it a policy tool. 

 The yields on rouble-denominated instruments started to slide after the central bank stopped curbing the rouble's strength making investments to hard currency less attractive and pushing banks to invest to treasuries or to extend more loans to the economy. 

 "This is an administrative rate cut that sets no benchmark to the market but it confirms their policy to reduce the rates on rouble denominated instruments," Sergei Shchepilov, a dealer at Reiffeisen Bank said. 

 The refinancing rate, which in most economies is a key tool in regulating liquidity, stopped being effective in Russia after the 1998 economic crisis which deprived commercial banks of the government securities market. 

 Since then, the market in government paper has been growing but is still seen too low to soak up much funds. 

 The new administration of the central bank, which took over last March, pledged that the central bank would become the focal point for setting rates and regulating money supply. 

 Until recently, Russia's central bank regulated money supply through intervention rather than rates. 

 The refinancing rate was last changed in August 2002, when it was cut from 23 percent. Last year the central bank cut the refinancing rate three times.

title: Russian rouble falls as liquidity fears ease.
text:
MOSCOW, Jan 30 (Reuters) - A rouble rally against the dollar lost some of its steam on Thursday when money supply data eased concern about an end of month liquidity squeeze, pushing the Russian currency to its lowest level in six trading days. 

 The Russian currency fell 2.24 kopecks in official early trade  to a weighted average for settlement today of 31.8224 to the dollar from 31.8000 on Wednesday. 

 The rouble has firmed in recent weeks, fuelled by high global crude prices that have boosted oil-rich Russia's export revenues. The central bank has intervened on several occasions to cap the rouble's rise. Russia is the world's second-biggest oil exporter. 

 Adding to the Russian currency's strength were concerns that the rouble supply would dry up at the end of this month when local firms must make tax payments and banks have to meet reserve requirements. 

 "(But) overnight lending rates eased ...indicating that the rouble supply is not that bad for the end of the month," said Sergei Shchepilov, a dealer at Raiffeisen Bank. 

 By 1140 GMT rouble overnight rates hovered at 3.75/5.75 percent as the central bank's data showed that banks' balances on their correspondent accounts  leapt to 91.9 billion roubles from 76.1 billion roubles on Wednesday. 

 Shchepilov said that the central bank's dollar purchases have helped to steady the market, hit earlier this month when two Russian oil firms drained almost 60 billion roubles to pay for a stake in a rival producer. 

 The central bank, which has been keeping a tight grip on the foreign exchange market over past four trading days by buying dollars to contain the rouble at 31.80, did not intervene on Thursday. 

 Igor Bogdanchik, a dealer at Dialog Optim bank said that the rouble could ease another kopeck or so on Friday to about 31.83-31.84. "Market liquidity is now enough to believe that the rouble will not appreciate," he said. 

 On the interbank market, roubles for Friday delivery  were quoted at 31.8250/31.8350 at 1125 GMT compared to 31.8175/31.8225 at Wednesday's close.

title: Russia cenbank steps in again to halt rouble rise.
text:
MOSCOW, Jan 29 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank intervened for the fourth straight trading days on Wednesday to halt a rouble rally against the dollar that has been fuelled by oil export earnings. 

 The Russian currency barely moved in official early trade  and stood at a weighted average for settlement today of 31.8000 to the dollar compared to 31.8001 on Tuesday. 

 Dealers traced the rouble's steadiness to the efforts of the central bank which bought at least $200 million on Wednesday. 

 "A strong supply of hard currency revenues from exports is balanced by the central bank's buying," said Valery Petrov, head of research at Rosbank. 

 "This foreign exchange market stability is making it difficult for other market participants to bet on a higher or lower dollar rate." 

 The rouble has been propelled by oil-rich Russia's hefty foreign trade surplus. Oil prices have soared on fears that a war in Iraq could lead to supply disruptions. 

 The central bank tries to contain the rouble's strength, often blamed for blunting the competitive edge of local producers, by buying dollars and putting them in its reserves. 

 Dealers expected the rouble to remain steady to moderately lower against the dollar over the next few sessions if the central bank continued to resist its rise. 

 "Export revenues keep on flooding the market and the dollar would dive (against the rouble) the very moment the central bank withdrew," said Artem Roshchin at Aljba Alliance bank. 

 They said there seemed to be little room for an abrupt drop in the value of the rouble given high crude prices and the dollar's weakness against the euro amid fears of a war in Iraq. 

 On the interbank market, another forum for foreign currency trade, roubles for Thursday delivery  were quoted at 31.8130-31.8230 at 1125 GMT, almost two kopecks lower compared to 31.7950/31.8010 seen at Tuesday's close.

title: Russian rouble slips as liquidity squeeze eases.
text:
MOSCOW, Jan 22 (Reuters) - The rouble slid against the dollar on Wednesday as a liquidity crunch eased and Russia's central bankintervened for the second day running to soak up the U.S. currency. 

 The rouble fell 0.92 kopecks over the morning in the unified session of eight exchanges and reached a weighted average for settlement today of 31.8095 compared to 31.8003 on Tuesday when it rose 2.21 kopecks. 

 "Liquidity has improved but one could still feel the shortage of roubles. That keeps lending rates high and holds the market (dollar) from bigger gains," Alexei Bukleyev at Alfa Bank said. 

 Improved sector liquidity trimmed interbank credit rates to 5/10 percent by 1215 GMT from over 20 percent in the previous session. The rise was sparked when oil producers Sibneft (SIBN.RTS) and TNK took some 59 billion roubles from the market to pay for a rival firm being sold by the state. 

 Dealers said that interventions by the central bank helped to alleviate the rouble deficit. It has bought some $300 million from the market at 31.80 roubles since Tuesday. 

 But they added that the rouble supply was still tight because of government and Moscow city rouble-denominated bond placements and pending quarterly tax payments by large firms, such as gas giant Gazprom. 

 "Large taxpayers have a special schedule of tax payments and according to our observations make the largest part of payments at the end of January, April, July and October," ING said in a research note. 

 Dealers ruled out that rouble gains over the next few sessions as the upside seemed to be protected by the central bank at 31.80. They suggested it could nudge lower after a return of fresh funds from the central bank's deposits on Thursday. 

 "The rates are falling and that could generate higher demand for dollars," Andrei Lisyev at Dialog Optim bank said. 

 Low overnight rates usually indicate better sector liquidity and trigger the rouble's downturn against the greenback. 

 On the interbank market, another floor for foreign currency trade, roubles for delivery Thursday  were quoted at 31.8090/31.8175 at 1215 GMT, barely changed compared to Tuesday's close.

title: UPDATE 1-Russian cbank dlr sales hold rouble steady.
text:
MOSCOW, Nov 1 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble was barely changed against the dollar on Friday but dealers expected the national currency to resume its slide once the central bank stopped dollar sales. 

 In the unified trading session of eight exchanges, used to set the central bank's official next-day rouble/dollar rate, the rouble nudged higher to a weighted average for today settlement of 31.7646 against the dollar from 31.7701 on Thursday. 

 Dealers said the rouble was supported by intervention from the central bank which tightly controls Russia's foreign exchange market. 

 The bank has been propping up the national currency with dollar sales at 31.7850 for the second day, after rouble demand waned when local firms completed their tax payments on Thursday. 

 "Banks have no arguments to change the exchange rate views of the central bank, which has $46.4 billion in reserves at its disposal," Artyom Roshchin at Aljba-Alliance said. 

 Dealers said the central bank may have sold at least $50 million to soak up excessive rouble supply, sending overnight credit rates tumbling. 

 By 1030 GMT overnight rates dropped to 1.0/3.0 percent from over 20 percent earlier this week. Banks' balances on their correspondent accounts at the central bank rose to 103.35 billion roubles from 86.31 billion roubles the previous session. 

 "Looking back on the actions of the central bank, it seems that it favours a gradual depreciation of the rouble by 10 kopecks a month," a foreign bank dealer said. 

 "We will stay at this level as long as the central bank backs the rouble," he added. 

 On the interbank market, another forum for foreign currency trade, roubles for tomorrow delivery traded at 31.7875/31.7900 a dollar at 1030 GMT unchanged from Thursday.

title: Russia  rouble stable on fears of cbank  intervention .
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 22 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble was stable against the dollar on Thursday as banks were wary of possible central bank intervention to prop up the national currency, dealers said. 

 The rouble firmed in official early trade, which serves as the basis for the central bank's next day rate, to a weighted average for today settlement of 31.5711 to the dollar from 31.5735 on Wednesday. 

 On the interbank market, roubles for tomorrow delivery , stood at 31.5820/31.5920 a dollar, little changed from Wednesday's close of 31.5850/31.5900. 

 "Yesterday the central bank showed that it did not want to allow the dollar to go above 31.60," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexei Bukleyev. 

 "That is why, seeing this and expecting a rouble shortage at the end of the month, banks started selling dollars on their own and creating short positions." 

 On Wednesday, the central bank asked banks for quotes as soon as the rouble fell to 31.60 per dollar. Dealers said there was no evidence that the central bank had been in the market on either Wednesday or Thursday. 

 Bukleyev expected the rouble to fluctuate in a range of 31.57/31.59 range for the remainder of the session.

title: UPDATE 1-Russia gold/ forex  2002 reserves to inch up-cbank.
text:
MOSCOW, May 17 (Reuters) - Russia's gold and foreign currency reserves will rise only slightly above their current record level of $40 billion by the end of 2002, central bank chairman Sergei Ignatyev said on Friday. 

 "(They) will not be much higher than now by the end of the year, otherwise we shall have problems with sterilisation (of money supply)," Ignatyev told reporters. 

 The main source of dollars for the reserves is revenues of exporters, mainly oil firms. The reserves rose significantly over the last several weeks as the situation on the energy market improved. 

 But by printing roubles to scoop up the petrodollars, the central bank risks pushing up inflation. The government wants to cut consumer price inflation to 14-16 percent this year from 18.6 percent last year. 

 Apart from interventions on the foreign exchange market, Russia uses its foreign currency and gold reserves to pay foreign debt. Russia is to pay the Paris Club of state lenders in the second half of this year as well as interest on several Eurobonds.

title: UPDATE 1-Russian rouble slides amid dollar demand.
text:
MOSCOW, April 1 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble fell against the dollar on Monday as end-of-the-quarter rouble deficit was over and the central bank moved fast to send a notice it will not allow it to fall beyond 31.20 for now. 

 "The overnight rouble rates eased and the central bank started offering dollars for tomorrow delivery at 31.20," said Mikhail Mikhalyov, the head of the foreign currency department at Zenit Bank. 

 The Bank of Russia regulates rouble supply through interventions rather than rates. It holds a tight grip on local foreign currency exchange market and immediately steps in when there is need to stamp out volatility. 

 In the unified trading session of eight exchanges, which usually serves as the basis for the central bank's next day rouble/dollar rate the rouble eased to a weighted average for today's settlement of 31.1741 from 31.1192 on Friday. 

 The central bank fixed the official exchanged rate for Tuesday at that level, 31.1741 to the dollar. 

 The currency traded within a band of 31.1650-31.1800, with the last deal clinched at 31.1765. Deals worth $64.4 million were registered. 

 "The rouble broke through 31.20 early but the central bank came out offering dollars at 31.20 (for today settlement) on interbank market. It gave a signal to the market as to what the level would be for now," said Artyom Roshchin, a trader with Aljba Alliance Bank. 

 On the interbank market, another forum in currency trade, the rouble for next day delivery stood at 31.1940/31.2040 a dollar at 1030 GMT, versus 31.1995 at Friday's close. 

 Dealers saw the rouble easing slightly on Tuesday as grabbing dollars while overnight rates remained low looked attractive. They expected no abrupt rouble fall. 

 "I don't think that (dollar) quotes will go much higher during the rest of the session and tomorrow everything will depend on the central bank but I am not expecting big changes," Mikhalyov added. 

 The overnight rouble credit rates fell to 3.00/5.00 percent by 1300 GMT from 8.0/10.0 percent in the early hours of trade.

title: UPDATE 1- Russia  rouble firms on heavy cbank  intervention .
text:
MOSCOW, Dec 18 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank on Tuesday carried out one of its heaviest interventions in recent months to help the rouble after a slump that had fuelled concern about the bank's ability to defend the currency, dealers said. 

 The rouble firmed slightly against the dollar in key dealings after a 12-kopeck tumble to a fresh low on Monday on concern about lower oil prices. 

 The rouble's weighted average in a unified session of eight exchanges edged up to 30.2769 a dollar from 30.3046. 

 "The only reason for the dollar fall is the central bank," said Metallinvestbank dealer Alexander Panasenko. 

 Based on the session the central bank hiked its official next day rate to 30.28 roubles per dollar from the 30.30. 

 Interbank roubles for tomorrow settlement were also firmer, quoted at 30.2825/30.2925 per dollar by 1335 GMT compared with 30.41/30.42 at the end of Monday trade. 

 Dealers estimated central bank intervention at $300-$550 million on the interbank market, where the central bank offered the dollar initially at about 30.41 and later at 30.29. 

 The central bank declined to comment. 

 Dealers have said the central bank has been spending about $100 million a day since mid-November to support the rouble and increased its intervention to $200-$250 million on Monday. 

 END YEAR VOLATILITY 

 Moscow Narodny Bank dealer Vasily Ushakov said that despite the recent drop he saw no reason to worry about the stability of the rouble. "The market is usually volatile at the end of the year," he said. 

 Bank Zenit chief economist Alexander Karpov added that the market was in the mood to see the rouble move down even further due to higher liquidity. 

 Banks' balances on correspondent accounts at the central bank , an indicator of liquidity, rose to 84.57 billion roubles from 71.31 billion roubles on Monday. 

 But dealers said the fate of the rouble depended fully on the central bank's actions as it maintain its tight control of foreign exchange trade. 

 Panasenko said the rouble could lose another five to eight kopecks to the dollar if the central bank left the market. 

 "(But) I think the central bank will continue to intervene," Karpov said about the interbank market. 

Intervention has been blamed for a $2.5 billion fall in central bank reserves over two weeks. They were reported at $36.1 billion by the end of the first week in December. 

 However, Troika Dialog chief economist Oleg Vyugin said the central bank was likely to work to maintain gold and foreign exchange reserves at current levels. 

 "The danger of a further decline is minimal, as banks are likely to sell off currency before end December to ensure salary and tax payments," former first deputy finance minister said in a note to clients.

title: UPDATE 1-Russia rouble falls past key level, hit by oil.
text:
MOSCOW, Dec 7 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble broke through the key psychological level of 30 against the dollar on the interbank market on Friday as the central bank finally gave up support of the currency above that level amid weaker oil prices. 

 Roubles for tomorrow delivery stood at 30.0675/30.0775 per dollar at 1320 GMT on the interbank market after 29.9410/29.9510 at Tuesday's close. 

 The currency eased only slightly in morning trade, monitored closely by the central bank as it bases its official rate on this session, but it later broke through 30 on the interbank. 

 Dealers said the move had come after the central bank removed its offer of 29.95 rouble to the dollar, a rate at which it had supported the national currency in the last two weeks. 

 The central bank has been intervening heavily to support the national currency in the last two weeks at 29.95. Analysts and dealers estimated interventions at $1.5 billion-$2 billion. 

 The spending has come amid falling reserves, down $1.3 billion in the latest week after a big Eurobond repayment, and as banks have lots of free roubles. 

 "If there is no trust below 30 roubles per dollar it eventually becomes very expensive to support it. Basically, speculation made the central bank unable to support it at that level," said Peter Westin, a senior economist at Aton. 

 Analysts said the rouble was giving in to lowering prices for oil, Russia's key earner of hard currency, but which has slumped on fears of global recession from around $27 dollars per barrel in early September to around $19 a barrel now. 

 "What we are seeing now is market expectations for a quicker fall of the rouble due to changing prospects for 2002 on the whole and for the trade balance and export revenues," said Yuliya Tseplyayeva, an analyst at ING Barings. 

 PRECIOUS RESERVES 

 Dealers said the rate at the unified session, so called as it brings together eight currency exchanges across Russia, had stayed above 30 as the central bank had intervened with dollar sales of some $70-80 million at 29.9549 roubles per dollar. 

 This allowed the bank to keep the rouble's average rate at the session, which serves as the base for the official next-day rate, at 29.9527 per dollar . 

 This was after a previous 29.9165. Trade volume at the Friday unified session was a high $150 million and the official rate was set at 29.95 roubles per dollar after 29.92 . 

 "People will start to look at the oil price. I believe the rouble will be under new pressure," Westin said. 

 Tseplyayeva also forecast a further fall in the central bank's reserves, last registered at $37.3 billion as of November 30, down $1.3 billion from the previous week although the bank said this was due to the redemption of a $1 billion Eurobond. 

 "If next week shows a decline again, it will become a significant factor in the rouble's weakening," she said. 

 Dealers and analysts were mixed on whether the central bank would continue interventions, but were unanimous in saying the rouble would hold around 30 by the end of the year. 

 Ushakov said the central bank was unlikely to support the rouble on the interbank market above 30. "The way up (for the dollar) is open," Ushakov said, but thought the bank would remain a rouble buyer on the key rate-setting unified session. (Additional reporting by Artyom Danielyan).

title: Rouble breaks key 30/dlr level, more pressure ahead.
text:
MOSCOW, Dec 7 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble broke through 30 to the dollar on the interbank market on Friday, seen as a key psychological level as this is the central bank's minimum desired year-end rate for the currency. 

 The currency eased only slightly in morning trade, monitored closely by the central bank as it bases its official rate on this session, but it later broke through 30 on the interbank. 

 Dealers said the move had come after the central bank removed its offer of 29.95 rouble to the dollar, a rate at which it had supported the national currency in the last two weeks. 

 Roubles for tomorrow delivery stood at 30.0375/30.0475 per dollar at 1050 GMT on the interbank market after 29.9410/29.9510 at Tuesday's close. 

 "The only reason for the dollar's rise is that the central bank has abandoned its offer," said Moscow Narodny Bank dealer Vasily Ushakov. 

 The central bank has been intervening heavily to support the national currency in the last two weeks at 29.95. Dealers had estimated that the bank had spent some more than $1.0 billion over that time in supporting the rouble. 

 Dealers said the rate at the unified session, so called as it brings together eight currency exchanges across Russia, had stayed above 30 as the central bank had intervened with dollar sales of some $70-80 million at 29.9549 roubles per dollar. 

 This allowed the bank to keep the rouble's average rate at the session, which serves as the base for the official next-day rate, at 29.9527 per dollar. 

 This was after a previous 29.9165. Trade volume at the Friday unified session was a high $150 million and the official rate was set at 29.95 roubles per dollar after 29.92. 

 Dealers said the central bank was unlikely to support the rouble on the interbank market above 30. "The way up (for the dollar) is open," Ushakov said, adding that the bank would probably maintain its presence on the unified session. 

 He also said banks had plenty of roubles, despite the fact that their balances at the central bank, an indicator of bank liquidity, were falling and that tax payments were due. 

 Another dealer was more cautious. "If the central bank does not support the rouble at 29.95, the next stop will be 30.10 roubles per dollar, especially as (central bank chief Viktor) Gerashchenko has mentioned this level," he said. 

 He was referring to comments made by the central bank head in November, when Gerashchenko seemed to indicate that 30.10 was his floor for the rouble.

title: Russia  cbank sees no need for  currency intervention .
text:
ALMATY, Nov 15 (Reuters) - The head of Russia's central bank said on Thursday he saw no need to spend foreign reserves on propping up the rouble and that the currency would not fall beyond 30 to the dollar this year. 

 The rouble, which has been depreciating gradually all year as part of government policy, earlier hit year lows against the dollar as markets worried over falls in the oil price, a key revenue earner for Russia. 

 But Russian central bank chief Viktor Gerashchenko, speaking in the Kazakh capital, said he was calm. 

 "I do not think that by the end of the year the (dollar) rate will be higher than 30 roubles, although we will not spend extra currency to hold it within that level," he told reporters. 

 "For us the currency reserve is more important than a move of the rate above 30 roubles 10 kopecks or 29 roubles 95 kopecks. This is insignificant," he added. 

 The central bank earlier said its currency reserves were unchanged at $38.5 billion in the week to November 9. 

 The bank set its official exchange rate for Friday at 29.76 to the dollar, the lowest this year. The weakening came on the background of sharply lower oil prices and a row between Russia and OPEC on oil production cuts to support world crude prices.

title: Russian rouble slips, trade upset by U.S. woes.
text:
MOSCOW, Sept 13 (Reuters) - Russia suspended some foreign exchange trade on Thursday due to settlement problems in the United States following Tuesday's terror attacks while the central bank intervened to support a slipping rouble. 

Russia's main foreign exchange trading venue, the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange, (MICEX) said it had suspended afternoon trade. Dealers said problems also emerged earlier in the morning session when eight exchanges usually take part and set the central bank's next-day official rate. 

 Dealers said no regional exchanges participated, only MICEX. The interbank market was trading normally. 

 "Due to technical problems at the Bank of New York , which is MICEX's settlement bank for the U.S. dollar, trade in U.S. dollar instruments will not be held on MICEX's 'afternoon' SELT session on September 13," MICEX said in a statement. 

 The U.S. financial system has been hit since two hijacked planes on Tuesday rammed into the World Trade Centre, where many large banks, including the Bank of New York, are based. 

 In the afternoon session roubles are traded for today, tomorrow and spot settlement, although volumes are usually low. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement in the morning session ticked down to 29.4696 roubles per dollar after 29.4455 per dollar the previous day. The central bank set its official next-day at 29.47 after a previous 29.45 . 

 Russia's dollarised economy holds the second biggest amount of dollars in circulation after the United States. Banks and households, which have squirreled away an estimated $30 billion, are sensitive to any rouble/dollar hitches. 

 However, the atmosphere on the street was calm, with currency exchange booths quoting normal buy and sell rates, rather than the slashed buy rate some posted on Wednesday. 

 SLOW RUSSIA TRADE 

 Russian banks were too preoccupied with settlement problems to trade actively and the central bank had to intervene heavily in morning trade and on the interbank market, being virtually the only supplier of dollars. 

 "Trade is very slow. Everyone is busy with current payments. The central bank satisfied all dollar demand in the morning trade because banks failed to deposit dollars," a dealer said. 

 Trade volume in the morning session was $66.72 million. 

 One dealer said the central bank told all large banks it would buy any sums directly from counteragents at the average morning session rate if banks failed to deposit funds for trade. 

 Regional exchange officials said MICEX cut them off from trade at the central bank's request. They said they did not have a link with the Bank of New York, which gave details on the presence of dollars in trade participants' accounts via SWIFT. 

 On the interbank market, the rouble initially fell to 29.48-29.49 per dollar, but the central bank intervened at 29.47 roubles per dollar. Dealers said they expected a quiet market. 

 "There are no macroeconomic preconditions for a dollar rate change," a dealer said. "Tomorrow will be as quiet as today People will have to digest the situation and the United States has to put its payment system in order." 

 Metallinvestbank dealer Alexander Panasenko said the central bank would smooth any sharp fluctuations, although banks themselves would avoid them due to the settlement difficulties. 

 Interbank roubles for tomorrow settlement were 29.4700/29.4800 versus Wednesday's last deal of 29.47.

title: Russia  rbl firms to 29.25/dlr as cbank  intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, July 25 (Reuters) - Repeated intervention by the central bank helped the rouble to recover losses against the dollar on Wednesday and dealers expect the Russian currency to rise further, dealers said. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement firmed to 29.2491 per dollar on Wednesday from 29.2797 per dollar on Tuesday in a unified session of eight exchanges. Volume ticked up to $121.51 million from previous $121.42 million. 

 Based as usual on the session's results, the central bank raised its official next-day rate to 29.25 per dollar after a previous 29.28 per dollar . 

 "The central bank intervened actively today, starting from 29.29 roubles per dollar and gradually lowering the price to 29.25," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexei Bukleyev. 

 The central bank sold about $400 million on interbank market and some $30 million in the unified trade. 

 Dealers said the aim was to support the rouble and cut the exchange rate to buy dollar revenues from exporters at a lower price to boost its reserves, dealers said. 

 Russia's foreign currency and gold reserves stood at an all-time high of $35.6 billion on July 13, but central bank head Viktor Gerashchenko has said he wants reserves at $45 billion to provide for economic stability. 

 Dealers said the rouble would continue gaining in strength until the end of July, propped up by a traditional end-of-the-month need for roubles to pay taxes and by a shortage of liquidity after the central bank's heavy dollar sales. 

 "The banks may well have overbought dollars and it may trigger a rouble deficit. So the rouble may rise to 29.20 per dollar by the end of July," said Irina Zuyeva, a dealer at Derzhava bank. 

 However, dollar demand was likely to increase at such low levels and the rouble would fall to 29.30 at the start of August, she said. 

 By 0950 GMT, roubles for tomorrow settlement were firmer, quoted at 29.2400/29.2500 in afternoon exchange trade after a previous average of 29.2899. 

 Roubles were traded at 29.25-29.27 on the interbank market.

title: Russia rbl slips further but c.bank stems decline.
text:
MOSCOW, July 20 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank intervened in rouble markets on Friday after a two-day absence from trade and stemmed a recent tumble that saw the currency hit a string of record lows, dealers said. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement edged down to 29.2766 per dollar in a unified session of eight exchanges after 29.2715 per dollar on Thursday. 

 Based as usual on the results of the session, the central bank set its official rate for the weekend and Monday at a record low of 29.28 per dollar, just down from the previous 29.27 per dollar. 

 "Quotes on the rouble rose to 29.3000/29.3050 per dollar in the morning (on the interbank market)," said Alexander Karpov of Zenit bank. 

 "But then the central bank appeared and with its intervention it stamped out dollar gains...The bank also appeared in the unified session," he added. 

 Dealers said the central bank had started selling dollars at 29.3000 roubles per dollar, then later at 29.2950 and 29.2900 roubles per dollar. 

 They said total intervention was $20-30 million or more. Overall turnover in the unified session was $106 million on Friday after $90.18 million the day before. 

 Dealers were mixed on forecasts for the rouble over the next week, saying that it chiefly depended on rouble liquidity, which plays a defining role in foreign exchange trade. 

 Rouble liquidity tends to be tighter at the end of the month as bank settle accounts ahead of the start of a new month. 

 By 1110 GMT roubles for next-day delivery were quoted at 29.2700/29.3100 per dollar after a previous average of 29.2924 roubles per dollar.

title: Russian rbl falls to 28.65/dlr, seen stabilised.
text:
MOSCOW, March 2, (Reuters) - The Russian rouble lost three kopecks against the dollar in thin trade on Friday as fresh rouble liquidity hit trade, but dealers said they expected the currency to stabilise near current levels next week. 

 The rouble's weighted average at a unified session of eight exchanges fell to 28.6514 roubles per dollar on Friday after 28.6227 on Thursday. 

 The central bank cut its official next day rouble rate to 28.65 per dollar , after a previous 28.62, based as usual on the results of the unified trading session. 

 "The situation with rouble liquidity improved after a crunch at the end of last month and the first day of this month. New roubles appeared on the market...and the rouble fell," said a Russian bank dealer. 

 Dealers said the central bank offered dollars for sale at 28.68 roubles per dollar on the interbank market, indicating a possible new support level, but banks did not want to buy, considering the price too high. 

 The central bank bought some $50 million in unified trade at 28.62-28.64 roubles per dollar and was apparently buying dollars directly from banks, aiming to restock reserves that have fallen after earlier interventions, dealers said. 

Russia's foreign currency and gold reserves fell to $28.7 billion on February 23 after $28.9 billion on February 16, the central bank said on Thursday. 

 Unified trade volume was a thin $88.05 million after a previous $97.25 million. 

 Dealers said the rouble was likely to stabilise around the current level next week as both commercial banks and the central bank seemed to be satisfied with the current situation. 

 "It looks like demand and supply are balanced... They (the central bank) have managed once again to establish stability. The market does not want to buy more (dollars). Everybody is satisfied," the dealer said. 

 However, dealers said the rouble was likely to fall in March and hit 29.00 per dollar level within a couple of month as international prices for oil, Russia's main export, were sliding. 

 Rumours about a possible government reshuffle added pressure to the market and could push the rouble down, the dealer added. 

 By 1100 GMT, roubles for tomorrow delivery were weaker, quoted at 28.6750/28.6800 in afternoon trade after a previous average of 28.6614 roubles per dollar. 

 Roubles on the interbank market were quoted at 28.68-28.70 .

title: Russia  rbl flat at 28.68/dlr as c.bank  intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, Feb 13 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble stabilised against the dollar on Tuesday after a five-day fall as the central bank intervened heavily to extend long-awaited support and dealers said the currency may firm soon. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight exchanges was little changed at 28.6817 roubles per dollar on Tuesday after a previous 28.6808 per dollar. 

 Based as usual on results of morning trade, the central bank left its official next day rouble rate unchanged at 28.68 per dollar . 

 "The central bank is intervening at the 28.70 (roubles per dollar) level, and this means that it will not allow the dollar to rise beyond this level," said a Russian bank dealer. 

 Dealers said the central bank sold about $20-30 million in the unified trading session and focused dollar interventions on the interbank market, where it sold about $100 million. 

 "The main dollar demand comes from the interbank market, and it is more important for the central bank to satisfy it... and consequently, demand drops in unified trade," the dealer said. 

 Volume in the unified session slipped to $144.23 million on Tuesday after $147.16 million on Monday. 

 Dealers said the rouble was likely to firm to 28.65 per dollar by the end of the week in a market correction after losing 24 kopecks against the dollar since 28.44 last Monday. 

 Roubles for tomorrow delivery were a touch weaker in later trade, quoted at 28.6925/28.7000 per dollar in exchange trading by 1000 GMT after a previous average of 28.6810. 

 Roubles were quoted at 28.6860/28.7060 per dollar on the interbank market .

title: Russian rbl plummets to 28.48/dlr, cbank  intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, Jan 4 (Reuters) - Russia's rouble lost 32 kopecks against the dollar on Thursday in one of the sharpest falls since the 1998 devaluation as heavy central bank intervention failed to offset seasonal factors, dealers said. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at the key unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges fell to 28.4750 per dollar from a previous 28.1633 . 

 The central bank cut its official next day rouble rate, based as usual on the results of the morning trade, to 28.48 from 28.16 per dollar . 

 Dealers said the plunge was due to seasonal factors as clients snapped up dollars while hard currency supply was low. 

 "The week before and the week after the New Year mean a weaker inflow of dollars to Russia, because of Christmas holidays in the West," Alexander Zhukov, head of the State Duma lower house budget committee, told Ekho Moskvy radio. 

 He suggested the government was buying hard currency to repay foreign debt. "I think it is a temporary, seasonal phenomenon," he said. 

 Dealers said the central bank had apparently sold between $200-$300 million in unified trade and on the interbank market. 

 Moscow Narodny Bank dealer Vasily Ushakov said the rouble could have fallen to 28.70 per dollar or lower but for the central bank, as the unified session followed the interbank market which opened at 28.60 roubles per dollar. "The (dollar) demand is colossal," he said. "Clients are ready to take dollars at whatever price. Everyone feels it." 

 Dealers said the central bank met some of the dollar demand that had built up since December 27, the last unified trading session before the New Year. 

 They said the rouble had traded on the interbank market at 28.45/28.70 per dollar between December 27 and January 3. 

 Ushakov said banks' strong rouble liquidity had contributed to the weakening of the Russian currency. 

 Banks' balances on their correspondent accounts at the central bank, an indicator of the banking system's liquidity, fell on Thursday from Wednesday levels, but were still high at 122.63 billion roubles. 

 Moskomprivatbank dealer Ruslan Shcherbakov forecast the rouble would hold stable in the next few days. "Judging by how the central bank supported the rate, I think there is no reason for the rate to fall," he said. 

 At 1015 GMT roubles for tomorrow delivery were stronger at 28.4450/28.4600 per dollar after a previous average of 28.5678 per dollar on December 27.

title: Russian rouble ticks up but seen easing in September.
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 31 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble edged up on Thursday, supported by central bank dollar sales and demand for roubles to pad end-of-month balance sheets, but dealers forecast the rouble would weaken in September. 

 An unexpected rise in central bank hard currency reserves also supported the rouble, but was not expected to offset the predicted rise in the dollar. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, usually tightly controlled by the central bank, ticked up to 27.7531 per dollar from 27.7547 per dollar on Wednesday. 

 However, the rouble's gain was small and based as usual on the results of the morning session, the central bank left its official next day rate unchanged at 27.75 per dollar . 

 "The volume fell because banks were afraid to buy dollars as they need to close their balances at the end of the month," said Guta-Bank dealer Vladimir Kotyatov. 

 The central bank, which has intervened heavily recently to counter aggressive demand for hard currency, sold about $50 million, less than on recent days, dealers said. 

 Trade volume in the morning session fell to $195.91 million, higher than average, from a very strong $242.39 million on Wednesday. 

 Dealers expected the rouble to fall as soon as the central bank stopped selling dollars in order to replenish its reserves. Dollar demand was also set to resume in early September, as it usually does at the start of the month, they said. 

 A rise in central bank reserves, which surprised the market after the central bank's recent heavy intervention, would stabilise the nervous market. 

Russia's gold and foreign exchange reserves, which shrunk in the first half of August, rose to $24.1 billion on August 25 from $23.4 billion a week earlier. 

 "It's positive news and the market welcomed it. It will help to smooth the dollar rise, but won't reverse the upward (dollar) trend," said Nikolai Polunin, a dealer at Dialog Optim bank. 

 He said dollar demand would be sustained because the market expected an increase in federal budget spending after a series of catastrophes, including the sinking of the Kursk submarine and a fire which burned Moscow's television tower, the highest man-made structure in Europe. 

 Kotyatov said dollar demand would be spurred by fears of rising consumer prices inflation, based on higher petrol prices, and the rouble could lose up to 20 kopecks against the dollar within the next week, if the central bank allowed it. 

 Roubles for tomorrow settlement were little changed by 0950 GMT at 27.7800/27.7900 after a previous average of 27.7853 .

title: Pressure on rouble rises,  central bank intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 30 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank sold dollars on Wednesday in an attempt to defend the rouble which has been under pressure this week but investors' appetite for the U.S. currency is expected to continue, dealers said. 

 Dealers warned that heavy rouble supply coupled with seasonal factors could soon break central bank support and push the rouble down to 28.00 per dollar from the current 27.75. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, usually tightly controlled by the central bank, was virtually flat at 27.7547 per dollar from 27.7549 per dollar on Monday. 

 Based as usual on the results of the morning session, the central bank left its official next day rate unchanged at 27.75 per dollar . 

 "The sentiment is that a bull trend (for the dollar) has started and quite a strong one," said Raiffeisen Bank treasurer Sergei Monin. 

 "The central bank stepped five kopecks back yesterday and that increased the sentiment even more, even though the central bank did the right thing to cool the demand at a higher rate." 

 Roubles for tomorrow settlement had fallen by 1030 GMT to 27.7810/27.7900 after a previous average of 27.7641. 

 The central bank surprised dealers on Tuesday after weeks of tranquillity by cutting its official next day rate to 27.75 per dollar from the previous 27.70. 

 DOLLAR DEMAND CONTINUES 

 Seasonal demand for dollars from banks' clients and banks, for which the foreign exchange market is the only way to invest their plethora of roubles, could persuade the central bank to let the rouble ease more, for the sake of its dollar reserves. 

 "The central bank has had to intervene heavily for the last three days to stop the dollar from rising. But despite such massive intervention, high demand for dollars persists," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexei Bukleyev. 

 Monin said the 28.00 per dollar level would balance the market for some time offering banks a chance to take profits. 

 But Bukleyev said he expected the central bank to allow the rouble to ease by about five kopecks more in the next few days. 

Central Bank Chairman Viktor Gerashchenko said last week he did not see the rouble moving sharply in the next few months. 

 Bukleyev said the rouble would be more stable on Thursday, the last day of the month, when banks and companies have to pay taxes, but could fall significantly on Friday. 

 He said the market could be nearing an explosion as banks rushed to buy dollars as soon as the rouble started weakening. 

 "If there is any movement down (in oil prices), the central bank can spend all its reserves in two or three days, everything it has bought during the last half year." 

Central bank gold and foreign currency reserves have been slipping in the last two weeks for the first time since the start of the year reaching $23.4 billion on August 18. 

 "One of the questions is why should the central bank spend the reserves here (on the foreign exchange market)? Can they afford to spend their reserves to sterilise the rouble - that is the question," Monin said.

title: Rouble down to 27.75/dlr despite cbank  intervention .
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 29 (Reuters) - Russia's rouble fell five kopecks against the dollar on Tuesday as dollar short positions were closed, and the slide surprised dealers who said they had expected the central bank to maintain recent stability. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, usually tightly controlled by the central bank, fell to 27.7549 per dollar from 27.7047 per dollar on Monday. 

 Based as usual on the results of the morning session, the central bank cut its official next day rate to 27.75 per dollar from Monday's 27.70 . 

 Dealers said the central bank had apparently sold about $150 million, which was not enough to satisfy demand. They were reluctant to forecast which way the currency would head next. 

 "The central bank intervened several times trying to curb agitated demand for dollars and almost all its bids were gobbled up," said Moskomprivatbank dealer Mikhail Zhirkov. 

Central Bank Chairman Viktor Gerashchenko said last week he did not expect the rouble rate to change sharply in the next several months. 

 "We have been marking time for three weeks and decided on a (dollar) rise today. There were a few more short positions than long ones and today they are equal," a Russian bank dealer said, explaining the reasons behind the move. 

 Roubles for tomorrow settlement had fallen by 0845 GMT to 27.7650/27.7730 after a previous average of 27.7396 .

title: Russia  rouble flat at 27.71/dlr as cbank  intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 23 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble was unchanged for the second day in a row, and dealers said on Wednesday the central bank had again beaten off an attack on the national currency by selling dollars. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, usually tightly controlled by the central bank, was flat at 27.7148 per dollar. 

 Based as usual on the results of the morning session, the central bank left its official rate unchanged at 27.71 per dollar . 

 "There has been a strong demand for dollars for several days in a row due to seasonal factors, because the dollar usually rises at the start of autumn," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexei Bukleyev. 

 "Everyone is trying to accumulate long positions ahead of the end of summer." 

 Dealers said the central bank had apparently sold about $100 million to support the rouble. 

 Bukleyev said banks channelled most free funds to the market. 

 Despite the fact the central bank has been intervening heavily over the last several days, commercial banks' balances at the central bank, which indicate banks' liquidity, have been rising. 

 "The central bank is stubbornly unwilling to let it (the dollar) rise," Bukleyev said. 

 "If it (the central bank) keeps holding the rate as it has been, it will knock off the demand which will lead to a fall (of the dollar.)" 

 He forecast the fall could be by two to three kopecks. 

 "If it (the central bank) abandons (the market) one day...the dollar will start rising sharply, by about 10 kopecks a day before the central bank decides to fix it a certain level," Bukleyev said. 

 In afternoon trade, roubles for tomorrow settlement were slightly stronger, quoted at 27.7310/27.7370 at 0850 GMT after a previous average of 27.7439 .

title: Russia  rouble firms to 28.83/dlr as cbank  intervenes .
text:
MOSCOW, July 17 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble gained two more kopecks on Monday, rising to 28.83 per dollar , while the central bank bought its usual portion of hard currency, dealers said. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, tightly controlled by the central bank, rose to 27.8250 roubles per dollar from 27.8456 roubles on Friday. 

 Based on the results of the morning session, the central bank set its official rate at 27.83 roubles per dollar , up from 27.85 on the previous trading day. 

 "The market is too regulated, and central bank's tough pressure on the upper and lower level of the rate sets the usual changes," said Alexander Timofeyev, head of the resource management department at Mosneftekhimbank. 

 Timofeyev explained the low trade volume by the fact that most buyers had switched to the interbank market where they did not have to pay a commission as they did at exchanges. 

 Trade turnover fell to a modest $98.53 million after $126.33 million on Friday. 

 Dealers said the central bank had apparently bought about $40-50 million. 

 Timofeyev said the rouble would gain one to two kopecks a day until the end of the week, adding however, that a downward correction was possible on Thursday or Friday. 

 But he said 28.00 roubles per dollar rate represented strong resistance level. 

 Roubles for tomorrow settlement were also firmer in afternoon trade, quoted at 27.8274/27.8350 at 1030 GMT after a previous average of 27.8559 . ((Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow newsroom, +075 941-8520 julie.tolkacheva@reuters.com)).

title: Russia  rouble up to 28.05/dlr on cbank  intervention .
text:
MOSCOW, June 30 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble edged up on Friday, supported by central bank hard currency sales in a market awash with roubles, dealers said. 

 The rouble's weighted average for today settlement at a unified trading session of eight Russian exchanges, tightly controlled by the central bank, rose to 28.0516 per dollar from 28.0650 per dollar on Thursday. 

 Based as usual on the results of the morning session, the central bank set its official next day rate at 28.05 roubles per dollar , up from a previous 28.07. 

 Rouble liquidity is high although it is the end of the month and the half-year, when banks and companies pay taxes that usually absorb roubles. 

 "Even after taxes, banks still have a lot of roubles," said Vladimir Sokolov, head of the hard currency department at Rosbank. 

 The central bank sold about $100 million to push the rouble up, dealers said. 

 "Market participants are in the mood to use some of the rouble to buy hard currency which is happening," Sokolov said. 

 He forecast the rouble would weaken next week, to around 28.15. 

 Roubles for tomorrow settlement were firmer in afternoon trade, quoted at 28.0610/28.0650 at 1100 GMT after a previous average of 28.0787 roubles per dollar. ((Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow newsroom, +075 941-8520 moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: UPDATE 1-Russia c.bank head against artificially low rouble.
text:
MOSCOW, May 23 (Reuters) - Russian Central Bank Chairman Viktor Gerashchenko said on Tuesday the rouble should not be artificially weakened to help the government meet budget obligations but should fluctuate smoothly. 

 Gerashchenko was responding to a statement last week by Prime Minister Mikhail Kasyanov that a further strengthening of the rouble was not in the best interests of the economy. 

 "I understand the position of Kasyanov, with his responsibility for the budget, but essentially to finance budget spending by artificially lowering the rouble is ineffective," Gerashchenko told journalists at a bankers' congress. 

 "I am in favour of it (the rouble) moving smoothly, one way and another," he said. 

 Kasyanov's statement had jolted Russia's foreign exchange market, forcing the central bank to intervene heavily to prevent sharp losses against the dollar, traders said. 

 The rouble has since steadied and was set by the central bank for Tuesday at 28.30 per dollar after the previous 28.31 per dollar. It had slipped to 28.33 per dollar after Kasyanov's comments. 

 The currency has been supported by strong international prices for Russia's main energy and commodities exports. 

 Exporters are obliged to sell up to 75 percent of hard currency earnings. ((Anatoly Vereshchagin, Moscow Newsroom, +7 095 941 8520, moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 2000.

title: Russia c.bank says rouble support changed mkt mood.
text:
MOSCOW, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank intervened to support the rouble against the dollar on Monday and has succeeded in changing the mood of the market, a central bank official said on Tuesday. 

 "We carried out operations in volumes sufficient to change the mood of market participants," said the official, who declined to be named. "Those banks which buy dollars today in the Unified Trading System will be disappointed," he said. 

 The Unified Trading Session involves eight exchanges throughout Russia and its average rate serves as the basis for the central bank's official rate, which tumbled 10 kopecks to a new low of 26.49 per dollar on Monday. 

 "The situation on the foreign exchange market is under our control," the central bank official said. He gave no details of the intervention but said the central bank was a net buyer of dollars in November. 

 Dealers said the rouble would have fallen further on Monday were it not for central bank support. One said the central bank was supporting the currency at 26.50 per dollar and would probably try to maintain that level through the next few days. 

Central Bank Chairman Viktor Gerashchenko has said the rouble will finish the year at 27 per dollar. 

 ((Artyom Danielyan, Moscow Newsroom, +7 095 941 8520, moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1999.

title: Russian rouble firms to 25.54/dlr in volatile trade.
text:
MOSCOW, Sept 13 (Reuters) - The Russian rouble firmed on 

 Monday boosted in part by a rogue deal and apparent support from 

 the central bank, traders said. 

     The rouble averaged 25.5443 per dollar after Friday's 

 25.7036 in the unified session of eight exchanges trading 

 roubles for today settlement, and the central bank as usual set 


its next day rate	    at the average, 25.54, after 25.70.



    Volume in the session was high at $220.28 million and trade



volatile with deals closed in the range 24.5500-25.9999 per



dollar.



 "The market opened up softer today, but a short time after



trade opened there was a deal for about $20 million at 24.55 per



dollar...I think it's fairly clear this was a (technical)



mistake by central bank traders," said one Russian dealer.



    Officials of the key Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange



(MICEX) confirmed there had been a deal closed at 24.55 per



dollar. Central bank officials were unavailable for comment.



    The Russian dealer, who said such relatively large deals



were usually made by the central bank, saw the rouble on Tuesday



correcting to near its previous level, between 25.70 and 25.80



per dollar.



He said he also saw pressure on the currency after an



early-morning bomb blast levelled a suburban Moscow apartment



block on Monday, killing at least 34 people.



"There's been no direct effect on the rouble today, but the



bombing adds trouble to an already uncertain background which



has been encouraging investors to switch from roubles and rouble



instruments into dollar-related instruments," he said.



Renaissance Capital fixed income analyst Parvoleta Shtereva



hesitated to attribute the rogue deal to the central bank but



she said recent high volumes in the unified session were a clear



indication the bank had been intervening in trade.



"Volume in trade is far too high right now and there is no



reason for it except that the central bank is intervening and



that defies logic, especially because of factors like Russia's



positive trade balance," she said.



    Hard currency from Russia's trade surplus should be enough



to support the rouble but the currency has been easing recently.



    Shtereva said central bank intervention to boost the rouble



amounted to "giving away its reserves" to banks and would only



serve to further deplete its foreign currency stockpile.



    "The central bank has either lost the plot or it has some



cunning plan that it is getting ready to spring on the market,"



she said.



    The rouble was steady in afternoon trade, quoted by 1010 GMT



at 24.7600/24.8111 per dollar	    on MICEX's electronic SELT



   system after a previous average of 25.8022 per dollar.



    ((Moscow Newsroom, +7095 241-0101



moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Russian c.bank spent reserves on debt, not rouble.
text:
MOSCOW, Aug 3 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank spent $500 million in the third week of July to service foreign debt, not to defend the rouble, Russia's special envoy to international financial organisations said on Tuesday. 

 "The central bank simply repaid $500 million out of a $1 billion loan (to the International Monetary Fund)," envoy Mikhail Zadornov told radio Ekho Moskvy. "There has been no intervention on the market", he said. 

Russia's foreign exchange and gold reserves fell by $500 million on July 23 to $11.0 billion. They were down $1.1 billion for the month and at their lowest level since April. 

 Zadornov said the bank recently has not been actively intervening on the foreign exchange market, which has generally seen the rouble appreciate or hold steady against the dollar, and he called a downturn on Tuesday "a normal correction". 

 The central bank rouble rate eased on Tuesday to 24.22 per dollar from a previous 24.19. 

 Zadornov forecast the rouble would gradually fall in line with inflation but would not reach 32 per dollar before the second half of 2000. 

 Zadornov said an IMF mission was expected in Moscow on August 24 to review conditions ahead of disbursement of a second tranche of the $4.5 billion loan the Fund agreed last week. 

 The first $640 million tranche was disbursed at the end of last week, and the second tranche is expected in September. 

 ((Svetlana Kovalyova, Moscow Newsroom +7 095 941 8520, moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Russia G7 Envoy: Ruble Defense Depletes Ctrl Bk Reserves
text:
MOSCOW (Dow Jones)--Defending the Russian ruble has dragged down the central bank's reserves, Russia's envoy to the Group of Seven industrialized nations said Thursday. 

 "The drop of the central bank's foreign exchange reserves is nothing extraordinary," Alexander Livshits told reporters. "The bank used them to keep the ruble stable." 

 The central bank reported earlier Thursday that its gold and hard currency reserves fell by $500 million in the week to July 23 to $11 billion. That decline brought the fall in reserves to $1.2 billion in the past month. 

 The central bank refrains from comment on changes of its foreign exchange reserves or on currency market interventions. 

 The International Monetary Fund requires Russia to phase out administrative currency controls by September as a condition for receiving the next tranche of the Fund's $4.5 billion loan which was approved late Wednesday. 

 Asked what controls the central bank was likely to revoke first, Livshits said: "It could be the requirement for importers to make ruble deposits." 

 Trying to curb capital flight in the spring, the central bank began forcing importers to make ruble deposits before transferring foreign exchange payments abroad. The deposits, an implicit and heavy tax on imports, are returned only when importers show proof that their goods have arrived in Russia. 

 The measure was designed to discourage the use of false import contracts to export dollars from Russia. 

 Still, the central bank has taken some steps to dismantle other currency controls. 

 -By Leos Rousek; 7 095 974 8055; lrousek@ap.org 

 (END) Dow Jones Newswires 29-07-99

title: Russia rouble up at 24.21/dlr, IMF loan seen helping.
text:
MOSCOW, July 29 (Reuters) - The rouble firmed against the U.S. currency on Thursday, averaging 24.2104 per dollar versus a previous 24.2214, a day after the International Monetary Fund resumed lending to Russia. 

 The IMF's board of directors on Wednesday voted to release a first tranche of $640 million from an 18-month $4.5 billion loan, a move one prominent parliamentarian said would ease pressure on the currency. 

 "The credit will enable the government to make payments on its foreign debt without money from the central bank," Alexander Zhukov, head of the budget committee in the State Duma lower house, told Itar-Tass news agency. 

 "That will give Russia the opportunity to build up its foreign reserves, which is one of the most important tasks toward strengthening the national currency." 

 The central bank announced on Thursday that by July 23 its reserves had fallen to a three-month low of $11.0 billion, down $500 million from a week earlier. 

 Economists attributed the reduction to heavy foreign debt obligations and rouble underpinning. Some estimated the bank spent up to $300 million on intervention in recent days. 

 Mikhail Zadornov, Russia's special envoy to international financial organisations, was quoted by Itar-Tass as saying the government had plans to allow the rouble to fluctuate relative to the rate of inflation. 

 In Washington, Zadornov spoke to journalists after the IMF loan was announced but would not say when the rouble plans would be put into action or give any further details. 

 Over the last month the official rouble rate, which is based on the results of unified trade on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange's electronic SELT system, has dropped about one percent against the dollar under central bank support. 

 But inflation in the first three weeks alone of July was 2.2 percent month-on-month. 


The central bank set the official exchange rate	  for Friday firmer at 24.21 per dollar, after 24.22, three days in a row.



By 1120 GMT roubles for tomorrow settlement on SELT were quoted at 24.2301/24.2520 per dollar after a previous average of 24.2543.



Spot roubles, for day-after-next settlement, were at 24.2000/24.5000     per dollar. No spot deals were reached on Wednesday.

title: ANALYSIS-Kazakh economy seen weathering tenge storm.
text:
ALMATY, April 5 (Reuters) - Kazakhstan's decision to follow Russia's example and effectively devalue its currency may send tremors through the economy but they will probably pass more quickly than those shaking its giant neighbour, officials and economists said. 

 Kazakhstan, the latest victim of the economic crisis in Russia, on Monday abandoned its increasingly costly defence of the tenge in favour of a free floating rate. 

 A hint of panic crept into the markets within hours, with the tenge losing 13 percent of its value against the dollar in extremely thin trade. 

 But while the new policy may come as a jolt to the Central Asian state's 16 million people, it need not spell the same kind of disaster as a similar move last August did for Russia. 

 "The change will come as a shock over the next couple of weeks before a return to normality," said Madina Dushimova, research director at KazkommertsSecurities, part of Kazakhstan's largest private bank. 

 "The fundamentals are different for Kazakhstan than they were for Russia. There is no treasury-bill pyramid, not the same huge foreign debt, fiscal discipline here is much better and, most importantly, there is a government and a strong national bank," she added. 

 Keen to stress the distance from Moscow, Finance Minister Uraz Dzhandosov said that there would be no Russian-style debt defaults or moratoria and that the Kazakh banking system was better prepared to withstand the inevitable strain. 

 Pressure has grown on the central bank to act to stave off increasing competition from neighbouring countries, particularly key trade partner Russia, where the rouble has lost more than 75 percent of its value since August. 

 Resource-rich Kazakhstan, five times the size of France, has also suffered from the slump in prices for key export earners oil and metals. Its trade deficit has widened and foreign reserves have been whittled away. 

 Kazakhstan's first course of action was to support the tenge through regular intervention, ban imports of some goods from Russia and impose a whopping 200 percent import duty on goods from Central Asian states Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. 

 But Prime Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev said in a statement that the trade barriers had not worked and ran counter to Kazakhstan's policy of opening up its economy. 

 "To close the borders is economically virtually impossible and incorrect from a political point of view," Balgimbayev said. "Russia and our Central Asian neighbours are friends and it is not worth getting involved in trade wars." 

 Finance Minister Dzhandosov said the tenge would now be allowed to find its natural level in the hope that this will help producers and exporters to compete more effectively. 

 The bold move, which took many bankers in the commercial centre of Almaty by surprise, was broadly welcomed, if only because the old policies were clearly not working. 

 "The moment arrived where the price of supporting the tenge was too high," said Otbert de Jong, general manager of ABN Amro Bank Kazakhstan. "The decision was better than not doing anything at all," Dushimova said. 

 Kazakh producers and exporters will welcome the decision, although there is a price to pay in the form of a new rule requiring that all companies sell half their hard currency export earnings on to the currency exchange. 

Central Bank Chairman Kadyrzhan Damitov said that, in an attempt to avoid mass bank deposit withdrawals, savers were to be allowed to convert accounts into dollars at Friday's exchange rate of 88.3 tenge to the U.S. dollar if they did not withdraw for nine months. The tenge fell to 100.0 per dollar on Monday. 

 Companies will be able to convert 30 percent of their tenge deposits if they keep them in the bank for six months. 

 Pension funds with deposits held in tenge-denominated treasury bills will be allowed to change them for five-year hard currency bills. Compulsory reserve requirements for commercial banks have also been reduced to five percent from 10 percent. ((Almaty Newsroom, +7 3272 509410 moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1999.

title: Russian c.bank says rouble holds without support.
text:
MOSCOW, March 15 (Reuters) - Russia's central bank said on Monday that rules on repatriating foreign currency were keeping the rouble stable and that for the first time in years it had not had to intervene to support the currency in January. 

 The rouble crashed after August 1998, when the government was forced to let it float. It later ceased market interventions but introduced rules to bring hard currency to Russia by making exporters repatriate 75 percent of their hard currency earnings. 

 "The central bank intervened on the (foreign exchange) market all the previous years in January," Deputy Central Bank Chairman Viktor Melnikov told a round-table talk of businessmen and politicians at parliament's Federation Council upper house. 

 "In January 1998, the central bank had to throw $3.4 billion on the market to support the rouble. This year, for the first time in all these years, the central bank did not intervene in January as exporters' revenues held us." 

 He said the daily flow of hard currency into the country rose 40 percent between October 1998 and February 1999 and that the central bank expected the volume to rise a further five percent in March. However, he gave no figures or comparisons. 

 Despite the government order to exporters, mainly oil and gas and metals producers, the central bank's reserves keep shrinking as it helps the finance ministry make debt repayments. 

 Analysts also say Russia suffers from endemic capital flight but Melnikov said only 5.2 percent of hard currency due for sale in Russia did not return under the repatriation order. 

 He called for a law which would require a special permit for export operations, saying the current system allowed short-lived companies to launder money and export it. 

 Capital flight often takes place via fake import contracts, when the importer presents a contract to the government for permission to send cash abroad to pay for goods which never actually arrive in Russia. 

 ((Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow newsroom, +075 941-8520 moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Russian Ruble Ends Up On  Central Bank Intervention
text:
MOSCOW (Dow Jones)--The Russia ruble (RUB) strengthened slightly against the dollar in negligible volumes Monday, as the central bank again propped up the ailing local currency. 

 On the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange, the dollar for next-day delivery closed at RUB22.90, down from RUB23.06 Friday. Trading volume declined further to a paltry $22 million, from Friday's $25 million. 

 At the special trading session, restricted to exporters and importers, spot ruble closed at RUB22.90 against the dollar, marginally lower than RUB22.91 Friday. Trading volume totaled $130 million, down from around $150 million Friday. 

 Volumes on that session remained much higher than at the session open to all participants because the central bank obliges all exporters to repatriate 75% of their hard-currency revenues, a trader with a major Russian bank said. 

 Monday, the central bank set its dollar rate at RUB22.84, flat from Friday. 

 Sentiment was dormant, a trader with another major Russian bank said. 

 Asked to account for the strengthening of ruble Monday, the trader said: "God only knows. The central bank made that decision." 

 Volumes are likely to remain low, as traders failed to foresee anything that could perk up the market. Given the low level of activity, even Russia's battered central bank will likely be able to keep the ruble in a tight range, the Moscow trader said. 

 "If the volumes remain so small, they'll be able to do that as long as they like," the second Moscow trader said. 

 -By Paivi Munter; 7-095-974-8055; pmunter@ap.org

title: FOCUS-Russian reserves drained to three-year low.
text:
MOSCOW, Jan 28 (Reuters) - Russia's vital foreign currency reserves have slid to a three-year low of $11.6 billion, and analysts said on Thursday the twin causes were capital flight and payments to service the country's crushing debt. 

 The longer-term fundamental problem remained that people simply wanted to get hold of dollars and out of roubles with the central bank forced to keep propping up the currency. 

 Analysts said reserves may get support from compulsory hard currency sales by the country's energy giants. If not, the bank may boost capital controls or change the currency regime. 

 "The number is pretty difficult already now and you are looking at almost half the reserve level being in gold which the bank is probably unlikely to sell," said Erik Nielsen, executive director of emerging markets research at Goldman Sachs. 

 The level of $11.6 billion, recorded on January 22, was a fall from $11.9 billion on January 15. In the intervening period, Russia paid two coupons on its 2005 and 2018 Eurobonds, equal to $320.53 million. 

 The central bank's reserves are becoming the only source of hard currency for the government, which is scheduled to make $9.5 billion of debt repayments this year. 

 According to central bank data, the typical size of the gold component is around $4.0 billion, meaning the country has around $7.0 or $8.0 billion in cash reserves. 

 "We would think that if it does not start to pick up a little bit in the next three or four weeks one would have to take a sceptical look at exporters obeying the rules," Nielsen said. 

 To boost reserves, the central bank ordered exporting companies, chiefly the energy giants such as Gazprom and the oil firms, to repatriate 75 percent of their hard currency earnings. 

 The idea is to get some of the cash from the country's huge trade surplus, around $3.0 billion, back into the central bank. 

 Analysts conceded there was a time lag between the order being issued to exporters and cash hitting the central bank but said the fact the surplus was so huge and that reserves were still shrinking indicated capital flight. 

 "At least part of the problem and probably the major one is there is greater demand for dollars than their sale. The fundamental reason for that is that capital flight continues at such a phenomenal rate," said Roland Nash, an economist at Moscow's MFK Renaissance. 

 The central bank did not have many choices if reserves continued to shrink, analysts said. 

 It could stop supporting the rouble and let it depreciate or it could impose an exchange rate, much as in Soviet days when there was an official rate and a black market rate. 

 More capital controls could also be imposed, they said. 

 "I would assume that if they (reserves) fall below 10 or nine billion this would be alarming and maybe even change the exchange rate system," said one analyst. ((Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941-8520 moscow.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1999.
